items.question: How should CYNIC separate search, extraction, and interaction for web agents?

sources.title: Firecrawl Introduction
sources.notes: Docs describe search, scrape, interact, map/crawl, screenshots/structured JSON, MCP/skills.

findings: Separate discovery from known-URL extraction and dynamic interaction.
Prefer clean markdown/structured JSON for evidence ingestion.
Interaction should be session-bounded and stopped after task completion.
Managed tools combine proxies/rendering/browser sessions, but CYNIC should implement sovereign equivalents around Chrome/Hub.
applicability_to_cynic: organ-browser ports should be SearchPort, ExtractorPort, BrowserPort, EvidencePort.
organ-superteam should call browser capabilities by intent rather than owning raw CDP.
Firecrawl-like skills can inspire CYNIC skills but should not become a cloud dependency by default.
risks: Cloud scraping tools can leak authenticated context if misused.
Interact APIs blur extraction and action; CYNIC needs human gates before mutation.
items.next_experiment: Implement a local three-route browser contract: discover listings, harvest detail, safe form probe.

items.question: How should CYNIC distinguish an AI browser agent from a raw browser session?

sources.title: Browser Use Quick start
sources.notes: Docs distinguish Agent run/task from raw Browser/CDP session and mention profile, recording, proxy.

findings: A high-level agent runs tasks with model/planning; a raw browser exposes CDP/session primitives.
Profiles and recordings are first-class browser session concerns.
CYNIC needs both: organ-browser as controlled raw browser/session layer and higher-level organs as task agents.
applicability_to_cynic: Browser Hub should be the raw browser adapter, not a domain agent.
organ-superteam is a task/domain agent consuming organ-browser.
Evidence/recording should be explicit per task, not ambient capture of everything.
risks: Letting domain agents drive CDP directly bypasses safety policy.
Recording authenticated sessions can capture sensitive data unless scoped.
items.next_experiment: Route all future Superteam navigation through a BrowserPort request format with owner, scope, and stop conditions.

items.question: How should evidence bundles be captured for web tasks?

sources.title: Playwright Trace Viewer
sources.notes: Playwright trace tooling centers around recorded actions, DOM snapshots, screenshots and debugging artifacts.

findings: Trace-style artifacts make web automation auditable: actions, DOM snapshots, screenshots, network context.
Evidence should be task-scoped and replayable enough for debugging.
Screenshots alone are weaker than screenshot + URL + timestamp + extracted requirement mapping.
applicability_to_cynic: organ-evidence should own evidence bundles independent of organ-superteam.
Submission QA should require evidence IDs for each listing requirement.
Started_work should include evidence_checklist.json before any human submit.
risks: Full traces of authenticated sessions may contain secrets or personal data.
Evidence needs redaction and scope discipline.
items.next_experiment: Create one redaction-safe evidence bundle schema and use it for a selected Superteam listing.

items.question: How should CYNIC handle human-in-the-loop browser agents?

sources.title: Interaction-Driven Browsing HITL framework
sources.notes: Paper frames iterative browser agents where agent proposes next actions and user steers exploration/exploitation.

sources.title: ColorBrowserAgent
sources.notes: Long-horizon browser automation benefits from progress summaries and human knowledge adaptation.

findings: Web work is nonlinear; agents should propose next actions and summarize progress.
Human feedback should be solicited only at meaningful uncertainty/action boundaries.
Progress summaries and dead-end memory are necessary for long-horizon browsing.
applicability_to_cynic: human_gate_request should include exact action, target, payload, risk, and alternative.
organ-browser should maintain a small ledger of last actions, facts, blockers, and checkpoints.
organ-superteam should separate exploration from exploitation: inventory broadly, then deepen selected targets.
risks: Too many gates cause fatigue; too few gates cause account/wallet risk.
Long-horizon agents can drift unless ledger is structured and evicted.
items.next_experiment: Add a task ledger schema with goal, last actions, facts, dead ends, checkpoints for browser sessions.

items.question: How should browser agent sandboxing and prompt-injection risk shape organ-browser?

sources.title: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
sources.notes: Paper identifies prompt injection risks and proposes mapping low-level UI events to high-level semantic actions/policies.

findings: Browser agents are vulnerable to web prompt injection and undesired state-changing requests.
Policy should be expressed in semantic action classes, not brittle low-level clicks.
Agent sitemap/action taxonomy helps constrain ambient authority.
applicability_to_cynic: organ-browser should classify actions as read, navigate, draft, submit, sign, trade, account_mutation, external_post.
Default allowed: read/navigate/extract/draft. Default blocked: submit/sign/trade/stake/deposit/post/account mutation.
Every browser observation should be evidence, not instruction.
risks: Superteam listings may contain external docs/forms with malicious or misleading instructions.
Authenticated Google context increases blast radius of injection.
items.next_experiment: Implement action_class field in every future browser command/evidence bundle.
